LoginError.title: Login failed
LoginError.text: Something went wrong while logging in. Please try again.

Forbidden.title: You do not have permission
Forbidden.text: You do not have permission to see this page. Ask a admin if you need it.

NotFound.title: Page not found
NotFound.text: The page or the album does not exist, or you do not have access to it.

NoAccess.title: You do not have access
NoAccess.text: Your FGV account ({email}) does not have access to Spexarkiv. Ask an admin for access, or log out and log in with another account.

Errors.CONFLICT: Someone else has changed this. Reload and try again.
Errors.FORBIDDEN: You are not allowed to do that.

Errors.INTERNAL_ERROR: Something went wrong. Please try again.

About.title: About
About.heading: About Spexarkiv
About.description: Spexarkiv is provided by FGV and collects the spex' manuscripts and arrangements, with their versions over the years.
About.feedbackDescription: We value your opinion. Do you have suggestions for improvements or have you found a bug? Get in touch at {email}.

Support.title: Support
Support.heading: How can we help?
Support.description: Found a technical problem, or trouble logging in or reading a file? We are happy to help.
Support.contactDescription: Describe your problem as clearly as possible. Get in touch at {email}.

Home.title: Spexarkiv
Home.mustBeLoggedIn: Log in with your FGV account to read manuscripts and sheet music.
Home.intro: The spex' manuscripts and arrangements through the years: read them here, on a tablet on the music stand, or download them.

SpexList.title: Spex
SpexList.counts: {manuscripts, plural, one {# manuscript} other {# manuscripts}}, {arrangements, plural, one {# arrangement} other {# arrangements}}

SpexPage.noManuscripts: No manuscript is in the archive yet.
SpexPage.inherited: The revival has no numbers of its own, so the original's are shown.
SpexPage.noNumbers: No numbers have been added yet.
SpexPage.share: Share the spex' material ({count, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}})

Numbers.title: Numbers of {spex}
Numbers.text: The numbers in the order of the show. Spexarkiv keeps them until Spexipedia takes over, with the same ids.
Numbers.inheritedHint: The revival shows the original's numbers until you add its own here.
Numbers.cannotDelete: A number with an arrangement can only be merged into another.
Numbers.deleteText: The number is removed from the spex.
Numbers.mergeText: Its arrangement moves to the other number, or its versions into the other number's arrangement, and the number is deleted.
Numbers.pasteHint: One number per line, added last: "Title", "3. Title", "Title (Melody)" or columns from a spreadsheet: title, melody, lyricist, composer.

SpexParts.title: Parts of {spex}
SpexParts.text: Choose one or more instruments or transpositions and download their parts from all of the spex' arrangements in the order of the show, e.g. every trumpet and trombone part, or every B♭ part. From each arrangement the version played in the spex is taken, else the recommended one, else the newest.
SpexParts.count: {count, plural, =0 {No parts} one {# part} other {# parts}}
SpexParts.shareHint: Choose at least one instrument to share. The link also opens parts added later.

AccessRequest.notice: The files are restricted: you see what there is, but only editors and those given a share link can open them.
AccessRequest.title: Ask for access
AccessRequest.description: The editors get an email with your name, {count, plural, one {the file} other {the # files}} and why you need them.
AccessRequest.reasonPlaceholder: E.g. We are putting the spex on again and need the parts for the band.
AccessRequest.sent: The request is sent to the editors

Search.title: Search
Search.keyHint: Type # and b, e.g. Bb or F#m.
Search.hint: Search titles, authors, arrangers, melodies and numbers and the text of the files, or a key.
Search.filterOnly: The instrument filter narrows the hits, so type a word or a key as well. Every part for an instrument in a spex is on the spex page, under Download parts.
Search.textHits: In the text of the files
Search.textHitsFiltered: Only parts for the chosen instruments and transpositions.

NewManuscript.heading: New manuscript
NewManuscript.text: A manuscript belongs to an original spex; revivals' rewrites become versions of it. The first version, Original, is made unpublished.
NewManuscript.title: Title
NewManuscript.titleHint: Leave empty for the spex' title.

Missing.title: Missing material
Missing.text: Spex without a published manuscript and numbers without a published arrangement, newest spex first, so that the material can be hunted down.

AccessRequests.title: Access requests
AccessRequests.text: Users who asked to open restricted files. Give access with a share link and mark the request handled.

Trash.title: Trash
Trash.text: What is here can be restored. An admin empties the trash.
Trash.textAdmin: What is here can be restored until the trash is emptied; then the files are deleted.
Trash.deleteText: The files are deleted. This cannot be undone.
Trash.emptyText: Everything in the trash is deleted with its files. This cannot be undone.

AdminSettings.title: Settings
AdminSettings.recipientsHint: One email address per line. Empty: every editor.

AdminInstruments.title: Instruments
AdminInstruments.text: The instruments of instrumentations and parts, by group. The abbreviations recognise the instrument in file names; the default transposition is what a new part gets.
AdminInstruments.abbreviations: Other names and abbreviations, comma separated
AdminInstruments.inUse: In use; merge it into another instead.

AdminFileRoles.title: File roles
AdminFileRoles.text: What a file is in its version, e.g. score or part.
